items.stem: According to the passage, what happens when a piece of DNA is integrated into the genome of a recipient organism?
What is the main purpose of biotechnology as described in the passage?
Which of the following is an example of biotechnology according to the passage?
Based on the passage, which of the following best describes the role of restriction enzymes in biotechnology?
According to the passage, why is genetic engineering considered a significant advancement in biotechnology?
Which of the following is a key requirement for the multiplication of an alien piece of DNA in an organism?
If a plasmid is used as a vector to transfer a gene of interest into a host organism, which of the following must be true?
In the process of creating recombinant DNA, what is the function of restriction enzymes?
Which of the following best explains the importance of the 'origin of replication' in recombinant DNA technology?

A scientist is trying to create recombinant DNA using a plasmid and a gene of interest. She notices that the colonies do not produce any color when a chromogenic substrate is added. What could be the reason?
What is the term used to describe the process of making multiple copies of a DNA molecule?

A scientist wants to create a recombinant DNA molecule and is using a plasmid vector. If the foreign DNA is inserted into the tetracycline resistance gene of the plasmid, what will happen to the bacteria containing this recombinant plasmid?
Which of the following is a feature of a cloning vector that allows the replication of the DNA fragment it carries?

A student is observing a gel electrophoresis experiment and notices that the DNA fragments in one lane have moved farther than those in another lane. What can the student conclude about the size of the DNA fragments in the lane that moved the farthest?
A company claims to use biotechnology to produce a new type of pest-resistant crop. Which of the following mechanisms is most likely being used to achieve this?

A scientist is trying to clone a gene in a plasmid vector and notices that the recombinant colonies do not produce blue color when grown on a medium with a chromogenic substrate. What is the most likely reason for this?
A student is trying to insert a gene into a bacterial cell. The student treats the bacteria with calcium ions and then applies heat shock. What is the purpose of this treatment?
Which of the following is a method used to visualize DNA fragments after gel electrophoresis?

A biotechnologist is attempting to create a pest-resistant plant by inserting a gene from a bacterium. The gene is cloned into a vector, and the vector is introduced into the plant cells using a disarmed pathogen. Which of the following is most likely to be the role of the disarmed pathogen?
Which type of bioreactor is commonly used and is shown in the passage?
Based on the passage, what is the main purpose of a bioreactor?
Which of the following is NOT a part of downstream processing?
What happens to a host cell after it is transformed with a recombinant DNA that includes an ampicillin resistance gene?
Which of the following is a method used to introduce recombinant DNA into a host cell?
What is the role of the selectable marker in recombinant DNA technology?
A scientist wants to introduce a gene for pest resistance into a plant. Which method would be most suitable for this purpose?
Why is the use of a disarmed pathogen as a vector advantageous in recombinant DNA technology?
A biotechnologist wants to select recombinant bacteria from non-recombinant ones. Which of the following methods would be most efficient?
Based on the diagram of the pBR322 plasmid, which of the following is true about the selectable markers?
What is the term used for the specific sequence in a chromosome that allows an alien DNA to replicate?

A student is trying to insert a gene for pest resistance into a plant using recombinant DNA technology. They use a restriction enzyme to cut the DNA and a plasmid as a vector. However, the gene does not get expressed in the plant. What is the most likely reason for this failure?
Which of the following is a core technique that enabled the birth of modern biotechnology?
Which of the following is a feature of a cloning vector?
What is the main goal of recombinant DNA technology?
What is the purpose of making bacterial cells 'competent' before transformation?
A researcher wants to produce a large quantity of a recombinant protein. Which method would be most suitable for this purpose?
If a plasmid is used as a vector to transfer a gene for antibiotic resistance, what is the most likely outcome when the plasmid is introduced into a bacterial host?
If a DNA fragment is inserted into the tetracycline resistance gene of a plasmid, which of the following will happen?
In recombinant DNA technology, a gene of interest is amplified using PCR. What is the role of the thermostable DNA polymerase in this process?
